title: Dual of the Koszul resolution of a regular quotient
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and let f_1,\ldots,f_r be a finite Koszul-regular sequence in A [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r), B=A/I, C=I/I^2, and N=\operatorname{Hom}_B(C,B). Let K_A(f_\bullet) be the Koszul complex, regarded as a bounded complex of finite free A-modules resolving B. Then the total Hom complex \operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(K_A(f_\bullet),A) is canonically quasi-isomorphic in D(A) to the A-complex obtained from the B-complex \bigwedge_B^r N[-r] by restriction of scalars along A\to B. In particular H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(K_A(f_\bullet),A))=0 for i\neq r and H^r\cong\bigwedge_B^r N as B-modules. The quasi-isomorphism is functorial under localization of A, compatible with the induced B-module structure on the target, and the induced isomorphism \operatorname{Ext}^r_A(B,A)\cong\bigwedge_B^r N depends only on the ideal I, not on the choice of the Koszul-regular generating sequence f_1,\ldots,f_r.

proof.text: Write E=A^{\oplus r} with basis e_1,\ldots,e_r and let phi:E\to A send e_i to f_i. By the definition of the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], K_j=\bigwedge_A^jE, K_j=0 for j>r, and every K_j is finite free. The augmentation K_0=A\to B is a quasi-isomorphism because Koszul-regularity says H_j(K)=0 for j\ne0 and d_1(E)=I [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence, def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex].

For each j, the determinant pairing identifies Hom_A(\bigwedge^jE,A) with the corresponding complementary exterior-power dual, using the canonical exterior pairing [lem-sc-exterior-power-dual-pairing]. In the basis e_i this is the map sending a dual wedge and a primal wedge to the determinant of their evaluation matrix. Dualizing the Koszul differential therefore gives the cochain differential obtained by wedging with the covector phi; this equality follows by evaluating both maps on basis wedges and using the alternating determinant formula.

Write δ_j for the degree-one dual derivation sending e_i to the Kronecker delta δ_{ij}. Under the determinant pairing of Step 2, Hom_A^i(K,A) is identified with the span of δ_{j_1}\cdotsδ_{j_i}. Directly from d(e_i)=f_i and the Koszul sign rule, its cochain differential is multiplication by -\sum_j f_jδ_j. Evaluation on the top wedge e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r therefore gives an isomorphism of graded A-modules Hom_A^\bullet(K,A)\cong K_A(f_\bullet)[-r], which, with the sign conventions of Tag 0BQZ (total Hom differential as in Stacks, and d_{K[n]}=(-1)^nd_K), commutes with differentials when r is odd and anticommutes with them when r is even (for r=1 both complexes are A\xrightarrow{-f_1}A in degrees 0,1 and the map is the identity); in the anticommuting case composing with (-1)^n in degree n gives an isomorphism of complexes, so in all cases Hom_A^\bullet(K,A)\cong K_A(f_\bullet)[-r] as complexes. Since K has homology B in degree 0 and no other homology by Koszul-regularity, the dual complex has cohomology only in degree r. The degree-r determinant classes identify with the dual conormal module N=Hom_B(I/I^2,B), and their alternating products give H^r\cong\bigwedge_B^rN. The same formulas are preserved after localizing A at any g.

The determinant classes just used are intrinsic: the map from the top exterior power of the dual conormal module to Ext^r_A(B,A) sends a local dual basis to the corresponding determinant class, and the determinant change-of-basis formula shows that it is unchanged when a different Koszul-regular generating sequence of I is chosen. The same determinant formula commutes with localization, so these local identifications glue and depend only on I. Hence the total Hom complex is canonically quasi-isomorphic in D(A) to the restriction of scalars of\n\bigwedge_B^rN[-r].
